headline: AWS Cloud Migration: A Practical Guide for 2026
description: A practical AWS cloud migration guide for 2026 — the 6 R's, lift-and-shift vs re-architecture, a migration roadmap, the Well-Architected pillars, FinOps and the pitfalls to avoid.

itemListElement.name: AWS Cloud Migration: A Practical Guide for 2026

mainEntity.name: What are the 6 R's of cloud migration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rehost (lift and shift), replatform (lift and tweak), refactor or re-architect, repurchase (move to SaaS), retire (switch off) and retain (leave as-is). You choose one per workload based on its value, risk and how much cloud-native benefit you need.

mainEntity.name: Should I lift and shift or re-architect for AWS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually both, in sequence: lift-and-shift to get off the data centre quickly and reduce risk, then re-architect the specific components that genuinely need cloud-native scale, reliability or cost efficiency.

mainEntity.name: How long does an AWS migration take?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the size and complexity of the estate and the strategy per workload. A rehost of a handful of apps can be weeks; a full re-architecture of a large platform runs longer and is best done in waves.

mainEntity.name: Will moving to AWS reduce our costs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you optimise. A naive lift-and-shift can cost more than on-premises. Real savings come from right-sizing, autoscaling, managed services, savings plans and disciplined FinOps tagging and monitoring.

mainEntity.name: Can you help us migrate to AWS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Cloud migration and re-architecture is core to our enterprise work, including lift-and-shift and re-architecture of on-premises platforms onto AWS.
